RagShortTexts: The standing military of Armenia in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Armenia rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Armenia against overwhelming regional adversaries.

Spearmen in the front rank kneel in the dust with their shields raised, waiting for the cavalry charge to strike. The men behind them thrust their spears through the gaps as the horses fall, and each one looks for the officer's standard to know where to stand. A broken line in this fight means the baggage train will be slaughtered before the reserves arrive.

The staff has drawn the battle order for the highland pass, placing infantry in the valley and cavalry on the ridges above. Grain must reach the forts before snow closes the road. Send the plan under seal to the pass commanders, and keep it from the local chiefs, whose loyalty to the crown is still uncertain.
